newsitem.title: JAPAN: JAL 6-month profit to fall sharply - paper.
newsitem.headline: JAL 6-month profit to fall sharply - paper.

text.p: Parent current profit at Japan Airlines Co Ltd (JAL) in the six months to September 30 is expected to have fallen 77 percent from a year ago to about three billion yen, a Japanese daily said.

The projected fall in the half-year current profit is due to an expected year-on-year 28 percent fall in the company's half-year operating profit, the economic daily Nihon Keizai Shimbun said. The paper said it expects JAL's six-month operating profit to be about 18 billion yen due to higher fuel costs and a fall in its revenue per international passenger.
JAL spokesmen were not immediately available for comment.
